examples.en: Where did you hide the keys?
She hid behind the door.
Words don't matter, deeds do.
This painting is the work of a great artist.

note: for work as a job, use «посао»

examples.en: Our flight is delayed by two hours.
Have a pleasant flight!

forms: кунем се, куну се; pf. заклети се

examples.en: I swear I'm telling the truth.
I didn't do it, I swear!

tips: «Кунем ти се» means «I swear to you», and is common in songs: «Кунем ти се да си божанствена». The perfective is заклети се.

examples.en: Why are you angry at me?
This pepper is very hot.

tips: Of food it means «hot, spicy»: «љути или благи?» asks whether something is hot or mild (pasta sauce, ajvar, peppers). «Благ» is mild, not spicy.
«Љута паприка», «љута чорба» are spicy; of a person, «љут сам на тебе» means «I'm angry at you». The context tells which.

examples.en: That's unbelievable!
She was incredibly beautiful.
There was an accident on the highway.
Unfortunately, I wasn't at home.
Don't wake the baby!
I wake up at six every day.
It's getting colder and colder.
He gets nervous before an exam.
Everyone came except him.
Besides that, there's no news.
I need a little change.

examples.sr: У фирми је дошло до великих [про̏мена].
examples.en: Big changes have taken place at the company.
She sings very nicely.
Let's sing together!
The bomb exploded at noon.
This cake is a real knockout!
I made dinner for everyone.
Get ready, we're leaving in five minutes!
I need to tell him that personally.
Personally, I think you're wrong.
Are you hungry?
The kids are hungry, let's eat.
How long is the movie?
Nothing lasts forever.
My grandfather is eighty years old.
On weekends we visit Grandma and Grandpa.

note: masculine, but declines like words in -а

examples.en: How much do I owe you?
I owe you an apology.

forms: пређем, пређу; past прешао; impf. прелазити

examples.en: Cross the street on green.
Today we covered three hundred kilometers.
Your life is in danger.
There's no danger, everything is fine.
How many languages do you speak?
The doctor told me to stick out my tongue.

forms: договорим се, договоре се; impf. договарати се

examples.sr: [Догово̀рили] смо се да се нађемо у осам.
examples.en: We agreed to meet at eight.
Let's agree on it.

forms: свидим се, свиде се; impf. свиђати се

examples.en: Did you like the movie?
I think she liked me.

note: + dat.: «свидело ми се» - I liked it
tips: The perfective for a one-time «liked it»: «свидела ми се презентација», «свидеће ти се филм». For a lasting «like», use «свиђати се».

examples.en: I have a meeting with a client at ten.
The customer is always right.
Give me a sheet of paper.
All the papers are in order.

forms: gen. метка; pl. меци; gen. pl. метака

examples.en: The bullet hit him in the shoulder.
I have no more rounds left.
Take one step forward.
We're learning the language step by step.
Go out for a bit of fresh air.
The air in the city is polluted.
What's the difference between these two?

examples.sr: За [ра̏злику] од брата, он је миран.
examples.en: Unlike his brother, he's calm.

meanings: to take over, to take on

examples.en: I'll take responsibility.
Download the app for free.

tips: With files it means «to download»: «преузети фајл». In everyday speech «скинути» is more common: «скини слику на рачунар».

examples.en: I have a pile of work.
A crowd of people gathered in the square.
Make a wish and blow out the candles!
His greatest wish came true.
Where did you get the tickets?
I need to get a new phone.

tips: «Набавити» is to buy or get hold of a thing: «карте», «оружје». It doesn't go with experience: say «стећи искуство», not «набавити».

examples.en: Do you play the guitar?
The band plays every Friday.

tips: A musical instrument takes the accusative with no preposition: «свирам гитару», «свира клавир».
A band or club takes «у» + loc.: «свира у групи», «у клубу».
In traffic «свирати» means to honk: «Шта ми свираш, видиш да је црвено!» - why are you honking, it's red.

examples.en: You misunderstood me.
You spelled my name wrong.
You look a lot like your mother.
That's not like him at all.

tips: «Личити на» + acc.: «Личим на оца» - I look like my father. «Већ» sets up the contrast: «Не личим на оца, већ на деду» - I don't look like my father but like my grandfather.

examples.en: Forget the past.
That's in the past now.
Don't lose hope!
He is our last hope.
He's a very nice guy.
This cake is really delicious.

tips: «Фин» also means well-mannered, decent, pleasant: «фина особа», «фин мирис», «фин момак». English needs different words depending on the noun.

examples.en: I usually eat eggs for breakfast.
Boil me an egg.

tips: «Фарбана јаја» are dyed Easter eggs. In the game «туцање јајима» people tap eggs against each other, and one red egg is kept until the next Easter.

examples.en: We got on the wrong train.
That was a wrong decision.
My grandfather lives in the village.
This is a small village in the mountains.

tips: «На селу» means in the countryside in general. For one particular village, use «у селу» («у свом селу»).

examples.en: He is the only witness of the accident.
The witness was called to court.
The doctor is examining a patient right now.
The patient is feeling better today.
That's a well-known fact.
We have to face the facts.
Deal?
Stick to the agreement!

forms: седнем, седну; past сео; impf. седати

examples.en: Please sit down.
He sat down next to me on the bus.
Kiss me!
He kissed her goodnight.

examples.sr: Оклизнуо сам се и пао на [ду̏пе].
examples.en: I slipped and fell on my butt.
Get off your butt and help me!

forms: испаднем, испадну; past испао; impf. испадати

examples.en: My phone fell out of my pocket.
In the end everything turned out well.

forms: полудим, полуде; past полудео; impf. лудети

examples.en: Have you lost your mind?
Mom will go crazy when she sees the room.
I run in the park every morning.
Don't run in the hallway!
I have to finish the report by Friday.
I read the police report.
I'm very tired after work.
You look tired today.
He's a perfectly ordinary man.
It was an ordinary workday.
The bus passes here every half hour.
Time passes quickly.

tips: «Роба добро пролази» - the goods sell well; «пролази рок» - the deadline is running out. It can also mean to get away with something.

examples.en: It was a pleasure!
I'll gladly help you.
I've had a toothache for two days.
Brush your teeth before bed.

tips: Kinds of teeth: «млечни» (baby), «стални» (permanent), «секутићи» (incisors), «очњаци» (canines), «преткутњаци» (premolars), «кутњаци» (molars), «умњак» (wisdom tooth). The tooth fairy is «Зубић вила».

examples.en: We walked through the forest.
We got lost in the forest.
A glass of red wine, please.
This wine is from Fruška Gora.

tips: Red wine is usually called «црно вино» (not «црвено»), white wine «бело вино».
Red wine is «црно вино», white «бело вино», rosé «розе».
«Црно вино» is literally «black wine». Mulled wine is «кувано вино».

examples.en: My life has become a real hell.
Go to hell!

tips: Slang: the exclamation «Пакао!» means awful, a nightmare.

examples.en: Sign here, please.
He signed the contract yesterday.
What do you sell here?
The neighbor is selling an apartment in the center.
This is a very interesting book.
How interesting!
Merry Christmas!
At Christmas we go to my parents'.

tips: January 7 is the main family holiday. Greetings: «Срећан Божић!», «Христос се роди!» - «Ваистину се роди!». The day before is Бадњи дан (January 6).
Serbian Christmas is on January 7, with an oak branch, the «бадњак», and the first guest, the «положајник». The tree («јелка») is decorated for New Year, not Christmas.

examples.en: What are you hiding behind your back?
I feel he's hiding something from me.
Congratulations on the new job!
I congratulated her on her birthday yesterday.

tips: The pattern «честитати» + dat. + acc.: «Честитам ти Нову годину». It sounds a bit more formal than «Срећна Нова година!».
Congratulate someone on something without a preposition: «честитам ти рођендан» (not «са рођенданом»). Often it is just «Срећан рођендан!».
«Честитка» is a greeting card, «позивница» an invitation. «Хвала на лепим честиткама!» - thanks for the kind wishes.

examples.en: That's a real miracle!
No wonder he's tired.
Poor girl, she suffered a lot.
What a pathetic excuse!
That's a big lie!
I'm sick of your lies.
Our math teacher is strict.
She teaches at the university.

tips: In the vocative («Професоре!») it expresses praise and admiration, especially between men, like «мајсторе», «легендо», «царе».

examples.en: I doubt he'll arrive on time.
The police suspect the neighbor.

note: «сумњати у» + acc.: to doubt; «на» + acc.: to suspect

examples.en: What do you do?
I've been into sports since childhood.

tips: With the instrumental: «бавим се пливањем». The question «Чиме се бавиш?» asks what you do.
With the instrumental: «бавити се спортом», «музиком». The question: «Којим спортом се бавите?» - which sport do you do?
«Бавити се» + instr.: «бавим се спортом», «фудбалом», «музиком». «Играти» takes the accusative with no preposition: «играм кошарку», «играм шах».

examples.en: Whose phone is this?

examples.sr: Ово је човек [чѝјӯ] смо кућу купили.
examples.en: This is the man whose house we bought.
I prepared dinner.
I need to get ready for the exam.
He has great power in the city.

examples.sr: Учинићу све што је у мојој [мо̑ћи].
examples.en: I'll do everything in my power.

forms: gen. госта; pl. гости; gen. pl. гостију

examples.en: We have guests tonight.
You are our dear guest.

related.en: to be a guest, to perform on tour

examples.en: Damn, I forgot my keys again!
They say there's a curse on the family.
I missed the bus again.
You can't pass up this opportunity.
I bought new shoes.
Take off your shoes at the door.

tips: Usually used in the plural, «ципеле» (shoes); high-heeled shoes are «ципеле на штиклу».

examples.en: He's not a bad man.
The stepmother was very wicked.

note: not to be confused with «жао»: «жао ми је» - I'm sorry

examples.en: I was offered a job in Belgrade.
May I offer you a coffee?
I have a surprise for you.

examples.sr: На моје [изненађе́ње], дошао је на време.
examples.en: To my surprise, he arrived on time.
I looked for you everywhere.
There was snow all around us.
We waited two hours at the border.
Everything has its limits.
Mom is worried about you.
Why do you look so worried?
Use sunscreen.
The witness is under police protection.
Can you fix the bike?
I need to improve my chemistry grade.
He's a member of our club.
All the family members came.
Give me an example.
For example, we could go by train.
Did you do your homework?
Your task is to guard the door.
Everything is good in moderation.
He had a suit made to measure.
I rarely see him these days.
Are you still seeing each other?

forms: трудим се, труде се; pf. потрудити се

examples.en: I'm really trying!
Try to get there on time.

tips: «Трудити се да» + present: «Трудим се да проводим више времена са ћерком» - I try to spend more time with my daughter. «Потрудити се» - to make an effort (once): «Потрудићу се да дођем на време» - I'll try to be on time.
It takes «да» + present: «трудим се да стигнем на време» - I'm trying to arrive on time. Not to be confused with «старати се» (to look after someone).

examples.en: Remember what I told you!

examples.sr: Никако не могу да [запа̀мтим] његово име.
examples.en: I just can't remember his name.
Put that back where it belongs!
Go back to bed.
What an idiot!
Don't act like an idiot.
I like bread with cheese.
Buy some white cheese and kajmak.

note: «бели сир» - soft white brined cheese, like feta
tips: «Сир» is the young white cheese; the hard yellow one is «качкаваљ». Cottage cheese is «ситан сир» or «урда».

forms: поведем, поведу; past повео; impf. водити

examples.en: Take your sister with you too!
He took me out to dinner.
The sky is clear today.
Look at the sky!
I have to protect my family.

examples.sr: Ова крема ће вас [зашти́тити] од сунца.
examples.en: This cream will protect you from the sun.

meanings: to carry out, to pull off
forms: изведем, изведу; past извео; impf. изводити

examples.en: Take the dog out for a walk.
How did you pull that off?

tips: «Извести пса у шетњу» - to take the dog for a walk. The same verb: «извести децу на игралиште» - to take the kids out to the playground.

examples.en: The engine won't start.
My brother rides a motorcycle to work.

tips: «Мотор» is not only an engine but also a motorcycle.

examples.en: Freedom is the most important thing to me.

examples.sr: Изашао је на [слобо̀ду] после пет година.
examples.en: He was released after five years.
What is this button for?
He served in the army in Niš.
The picture hangs above the bed.
The temperature is above zero.
Would you like a cup of tea?

examples.sr: Кад сам болестан, пијем [ча̏ј] са медом.
examples.en: When I'm sick, I drink tea with honey.

tips: In Serbia «чај» is most often a herbal infusion («камилица» - chamomile, «нана» - mint). Ask for tea and you may be asked: «зелени, камилица, нана?» For a cold, the first advice is «попити чај».

examples.en: You deserve only the best.
He doesn't deserve a second chance.
Maybe it was fate.
You can't run from fate.
He's a very fast runner.
We have fast internet at home.
There's a chance I'll be late.
You have two options.

forms: повежем, повежу; part. повезан; impf. повезивати

examples.en: I think everything is connected.
We need to connect the printer to the computer.
Take a deep breath and calm down.
I'm deeply moved.
A big tree grows in front of the house.
The table is made of wood.

tips: The plural «дрвета» is correct, but in speech «дрвеће» is the usual word, a collective neuter singular: «много лепог дрвећа».

examples.en: I reported the theft to the police.
I signed up for a Spanish course.
Don't give up now!
He gave up on the trip.

note: «одустати од» + gen.: to give up on

examples.en: The police launched an investigation.
The investigation is still under way.
I get up at six in the morning.
I always drink coffee in the morning.
Don't make sudden movements.
He was a member of the student movement.
The queen visited our city.
She's a real queen of the dance floor.

examples.sr: Ишао сам у [сре̏дњу] школу у Нишу.
examples.en: I went to high school in Niš.
He's the middle brother.
How was the trip?
Tomorrow I'm going on a business trip.
Don't leave me alone!
He always leaves his things all over the house.
This is my wife Ana.
He came to the celebration with his wife.
I need your advice.
Take my advice and go home.
I work at a large company.
Thank you for the company.

note: for a group of friends, «друштво» is more usual

examples.en: In summer we go to the seaside.

examples.sr: Купали смо се у [мо̏ру] цео дан.
examples.en: We swam in the sea all day.

examples.sr: Могу ли да те [замо̀лим] за услугу?
examples.en: May I ask you a favor?
He asked me to come earlier.
In school I liked history best.
This city has a long history.
Be honest with me.
She was completely frank with me.
What's the score of the match?
I'm still waiting for the test results.
We're going to a restaurant tonight.
This restaurant has excellent fish.
I have a cold, my nose is running.
Don't stick your nose into other people's things.
We walk the dog in the park.
Let's go to the park after lunch!
Kids have a lot of energy.
We have to save energy.
The colonel ordered the attack.
Understood, Colonel!
Go this way, then left.
Does the bus come by here?
Look around, maybe it's somewhere here.
Don't go around talking about it.
Are you going to the party on Saturday?
We had a party at my place last night.
The judge pronounced the sentence.
The fans booed the referee.

note: masculine, but declines like words in -а

examples.en: Don't worry, I'll think of something.
Who came up with this plan?
I really love to travel.
Tomorrow I'm traveling to Belgrade.

tips: It is not only for holiday travel but for any ordinary trip: «аутобус путује 25 минута» - the bus takes 25 minutes; «У Црну Гору путујемо железницом» - we're going to Montenegro by train.

examples.en: The ring is made of pure gold.
You're pure gold!
It was just a joke.
I don't get this joke.
It's not your fault.
I feel guilty about it.
This is my daughter Marija.
They have two daughters.

note: bookish; in speech «ћерка» is more common

examples.en: She has very delicate skin.
He bought a genuine leather jacket.

tips: «Вештачка кожа» is faux leather; «кожни» means leather: «кожна јакна». «Вештачко крзно» is faux fur.

forms: опустим се, опусте се; impf. опуштати се

examples.en: Relax, everything is fine.
I need a vacation to relax.

tips: «Опусти се!» - relax! «Опуштено!» - easy, relaxed. After work: «Желим да се опустим» - I want to unwind; «Спорт је начин да се опустимо» - sport is a way to relax.
The imperfective is «опуштати се»: «Опуштам се уз музику» - I relax with music; «Среда је мали петак - време за опуштање» - Wednesday is a little Friday, time to unwind.
Ways to relax: «опустити се у спа-центру» (at a spa), «опустити се и искључити мозак» (relax and switch your brain off). Imperative: «опусти се!» - relax!

examples.en: He was driving at high speed.
Slow down, the road is wet!
Birds are singing in the forest.
Now I'm free as a bird.
Send me your address.
What's your home address?

tips: «Адреса» is feminine: «нова адреса».

examples.en: First I have breakfast, then I go to work.

examples.sr: Ушао је и [за̀тӣм] сео поред мене.
examples.en: He came in and then sat down next to me.
Where is my bag?
I put the keys in the bag.
His father is very rich.
This country is rich in water.
I'm proud of you.
The mother is proud of her son.

note: «бити поносан на» + acc.: to be proud of
tips: A positive word: proud of someone or something, with no hint of arrogance: «поносан сам на тебе» («поносан на» + acc.).

examples.en: What is your goal in life?
The runners reached the finish line.

tips: Masculine: «циљ»: «мој циљ», «јасан циљ».

examples.en: A truck blocked the whole road.
My brother drives a truck.
I regret what I said.
He's always complaining about work.

note: «жалити се на» + acc.: to complain about

examples.en: Just shut up already!
Everyone fell silent when he walked in.
Do you have permission for that?
I lost my driver's license.
What are you doing this weekend?
On weekends we go to Grandma's in the village.

tips: Only Saturday and Sunday. A personal day off on a weekday is «слободан дан», a day off for a holiday is «нерадни дан»; «продужени викенд» is a long weekend.

examples.en: I dreamed about you last night.
I've always dreamed of a trip to Japan.

tips: «Сањати нешто» - to dream something («сањао сам да летим» - I dreamed I was flying); «сањати некога» - to dream about a person; «имати сан» - to have a dream; «пробудити се из сна» - to wake from a dream.

examples.en: Sorry, I made a mistake.
If you make a mistake, start over.
She's a good girl.
Come on, girl, hurry up!
Please come in!
You can feel free to ask me.

tips: «Слободно» means permitted. «Је л' слободно?» asks whether one may come in or take something. The answer is «слободно!» - please, go ahead.

examples.en: I feel silly.

examples.sr: Било је [глу̑по] од мене да то кажем.
examples.en: It was stupid of me to say that.
What's the program for tonight?
I installed a new program.

tips: «Програм» is masculine: «нови програм».

examples.en: I'd rather stay at home.
I'd rather drink tea than coffee.

tips: «Радије» is mostly used with the conditional «бих»: «Радије бих остала код куће» - I'd rather stay at home. «Радије не бих говорила о томе» - I'd rather not talk about it.

examples.en: She has big blue eyes.

examples.sr: Она је [пла̑ва], а сестра јој је црна.
examples.en: She's blonde, and her sister is a brunette.

note: one word for both dark and light blue
tips: The main meaning is «blue» («плава боја»); it also means light-haired: «плава коса» - blond hair, «плавуша» - a blonde woman.
«Плава коса» is blond hair, not blue. A fair-haired woman is a «плавуша»; «плав» itself is blue («плаво небо»).
«Плав» can also mean light or pale yellowish, hence «плава коса» - blond hair, «плавуша» - a blonde.

examples.en: We're a good team.
Which team do you root for?
The show starts at eight.
I have no idea what happened.

tips: «Представа» is a show, but also an idea or notion: «немам представу» - I have no idea.

examples.en: Both of them are good friends of mine.
I love you both.

note: for two men; for a man and a woman use «обоје»

examples.en: The answer is quite simple.
Don't be so coarse!
What a beautiful dress!
She put on a red dress.
He's a close friend of mine.
Where is the nearest pharmacy?
Tomorrow I'll visit Grandma.
Come and visit us in the summer.
The train is half an hour late.
We're traveling to Novi Sad by train.
I've always wanted to see the sea.
He's always been like that.

note: covers the past up to now; «увек» is «always» in general

examples.en: I got an F in math.
Our unit sets out at dawn.

note: in school 1 is the worst grade, 5 the best

examples.en: You passed the exam? Well done!
Bravo, guys, you played great!
Call an ambulance!
I have an urgent call for you.

tips: The short form «хитна» (for «хитна помоћ») means the ambulance: «Позови хитну!»

examples.en: He rarely shows his feelings.
What are you showing me?
I can't stand him.
Tomorrow I'll hand in my resignation.

note: «не могу да га поднесем» - I can't stand him
tips: In official contexts: «поднети захтев / пријаву» - to submit an application / a report. It also means to bear: «поднети бол».

examples.en: I don't eat meat.
Buy a kilo of meat for lunch.
I'm terribly sorry.
You look awful, are you sick?
How much is this house worth?
That movie is worth watching.

tips: «Вредети» means to be worth or to have value: «Вреди да се проба» - it's worth a try.

examples.en: Give me a piece of bread.
How much does one piece cost?
We climbed to the top of the mountain.
This pizza is the best!

tips: «Врх» also means an arrowhead, the tip of an iceberg, and, colloquially, «top, great» («врх!»). «На врх језика ми је» - it's on the tip of my tongue.
«Врх!» is colloquial for «awesome!»: «Време је данас врх!» - the weather is great today. «Топ» and «екстра» are used the same way.

examples.en: Our mission succeeded.
He was on a secret mission.
Blow out the candles and make a wish!
I wished him a good trip.
Careful, the knife is sharp.
Cut the bread with this knife.
Don't forget to take an umbrella.
What should I take on the trip?
Mom is in the kitchen.
I love Italian cuisine.
He received an award for best film.
This is your reward for the effort.
I'm in love with you.
She's madly in love.

forms: gen. метра; pl. метри, gen. pl. метара

examples.en: He's almost two meters tall.
The shop is a hundred meters from here.

tips: «Метар» is also a tape measure («тракасти метар»): «треба ми метар да измерим зид» - I need a tape measure to measure the wall.

examples.sr: Ово је [де̏финитӣвно] најбољи ресторан у граду.
examples.en: This is definitely the best restaurant in town.
He is definitely not guilty.
Do you need anything?
Have you eaten anything today?

note: in questions and conditions; in statements use «нешто»
tips: «Ишта» means «anything at all», usually in questions and conditions: «Јеси ли ишта видео?», «Ако ишта знаш...». It is not normally used in affirmative statements.

examples.en: I get up at six in the morning.
I always drink coffee in the morning.

tips: After midnight it is already «ујутру»: 1 a.m. is «један сат ујутру». From 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. is «од девет ујутру до шест увече».
